Article Title: Devdutt Padikkal responds to no.3 debate with maiden century in Galle
Article Text:
India's Devdutt Padikkal (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Soon after pushing Sri Lanka debutant off-spinner Keshara Nuwantha to mid-off for a single, Devdutt Padikkal leapt in joy. He had just scored his maiden Test century — in his third Test and fourth innings — and earned a warm hug from India captain Shubman Gill , along with applause from chief selector Ajit Agarkar and head coach Gautam Gambhir.The fluent 134-ball hundred capped a fine comeback for Padikkal, who returned to the Test side after 22 months because of an injury to Sai Sudharsan. His unbeaten 131 (178b, 12x4, 1x6) helped India reach a commanding 288-2 on a rain-hit opening day of the first Test in Galle.‘DDP’ also became the first Indian batter to score a Test century on Independence Day. Padikkal’s ton ended India’s 19-Test, 35-innings wait for a century from No. 3 — the last coming from Gill against Bangladesh in 2024 — and strengthened his case for a longer run at the pivotal position, even after Sudharsan returns.More significantly, the 26-year-old showed that he could be the batter India need to counter their recent struggles against spin. He used his feet, rocked back quickly in the crease and employed his wrists effectively to neutralise Sri Lanka’s spinners. Padikkal had offered a glimpse of his form when he smashed an unbeaten 142 off 164 balls in India’s only warm-up game in Colombo.The left-hander, appointed Karnataka captain in Jan this year, has also been in prolific form in domestic cricket.India, however, lost opener Yashasvi Jaiswal (32) to a needless run-out and Gill (16) to a poor shot against Prabath Jayasuriya. They were rescued by Padikkal and KL Rahul, who added 150 off 255 balls for the second wicket before Rahul retired hurt with cramps at tea.Replacing Rahul, Gill struck a couple of elegant cover drives before throwing his wicket away, while Rishabh Pant kept the momentum going with an unbeaten 27. Pant and Padikkal added 52 for the third wicket in 67 balls.Gill had opted to bat after winning the toss in India’s landmark 600th Test, which is also Galle’s 50th. India picked wicketkeeper-batter Dhruv Jurel ahead of Sarfaraz Khan. Padikkal and Rahul, who have batted together regularly for Karnataka, complemented each other beautifully.Padikkal reached his third Test fifty off 81 balls, while Rahul brought up his 21st Test half-century from 127 balls. The Galle surface offered little assistance to the spinners, and the pair neutralised Sri Lanka’s main weapon, Jayasuriya, after he was introduced in the 10th over.
Article Summary: Devdutt Padikkal scored 131 (178b, 12x4, 1x6) to help India reach a commanding 288-2 on a rain-hit opening day of the first Test in Galle. The fluent 134-ball hundred capped a fine comeback for the Karnataka batsman, who returned to the Test side after 22 months because of an injury.

Article Title: British-Indian entrepreneur Amit Bhatia to acquire 30% stake in Liverpool FC
Article Text:
Ryan Gravenberch of Liverpool celebrates (Getty Images)

"We are making this investment because we believe deeply in Liverpool and its leadership and we look forward to supporting the club’s continued success for years to come.” Amit Bhatia

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

London: A consortium headed by British-Indian entrepreneur Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of billionaire Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal , has agreed to buy a 30% minority equity stake in Liverpool FC in an investment understood to be worth around £1.7 billion.Liverpool’s owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG), which bought the club in 2010 for £300 million, has entered into an agreement for the sale of a minority equity stake in Liverpool FC to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led by Bhatia and named after the year Liverpool was founded. The consortium has investments from Bhatia and the Mittal Family Trusts; venture capital firm K5 Sports, with Amazon founder Jeff Bezos as the lead investor; and EE Capital, the family office of Eduardo Saverin, the billionaire co-founder of Facebook, and his wife Elaine.FSG will continue to retain majority ownership and operational control of Liverpool FC, the world’s fourth most valuable football club. Once the investment deal has been approved, Bhatia, a former director at Queens Park Rangers who relinquished his stake in the club last month, will become Liverpool’s new vice-chairman.Bhatia said: “To be welcomed as a partner in a club of this stature is a huge privilege. We are making this investment because we believe deeply in Liverpool and its leadership, and we look forward to supporting the club’s continued success for years to come.”Spirit of Shankly, the official supporters’ union for Liverpool FC, said: “We will be seeking engagement to understand better what this sale and consequent changes will mean for the future of LFC and its fans. It is vital for the game in general that football clubs are run sustainably, as LFC has been, and not an arms race funded by mega-rich individuals or state-backed entities.”
Article Summary: A consortium headed by British-Indian entrepreneur Amit Bhatia has agreed to buy a 30% minority equity stake in Liverpool FC. The investment is understood to be worth around £1.7 billion. Liverpool’s owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG), which bought the club in 2010 for £300 million, has entered into an agreement for the sale.

Article Title: Feet moving, mind clear: How Devdutt Padikkal cracked spin puzzle
Article Text:
Devdutt Padikkal (BCCI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The fabulous, fluent 131 not out off 178 balls against Sri Lanka on Saturday was more than Devdutt Padikkal’s maiden Test century. It was another comeback chapter for the resilient 26-year-old, who had waited 632 days for another India appearance.Padikkal’s career has been marked by such recoveries. After a modest 119 runs in five matches in the 2023-24 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, he responded with 465 runs at 155 in the Vijay Hazare Trophy and 556 at 92.66 in the Ranji Trophy , including three centuries.The last eight months have been particularly productive. Named Karnataka captain in Jan, Padikkal scored 543 runs at 60.33 in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy, including two hundreds. His back-to-back IPL titles with RCB have also added to his experience, including the opportunity to work with Virat Kohli Playing his first Test since Perth in Nov 2024, Padikkal became the first Indian batter to score a Test century on Independence Day and ended a 19-Test, 35-innings wait for a No. 3 hundred.Coming off an unbeaten century in the warm-up game, he began confidently, hitting debutant off-spinner Keshara Nuwantha for four before launching Prabhat Jayasuriya over long-on for six. His ability to use the crease, play off the back foot and attack spin stood out on a slow Galle surface.Former India batter Sanjay Manjrekar hailed him as a “godsend for India” against spin, saying his defence, ability to rotate the strike and attacking shots made him ideally suited to turning tracks.Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak credited Padikkal’s preparation, revealing that he had worked extensively at the BCCI Centre of Excellence on his back-foot game, stepping out and playing sweeps.“I am so happy for him because he was actually waiting for his chance. The way he played here and in the warmup match, it’s really encouraging,” Kotak said. “We tried to work on step-out, sweep besides the back-foot game. A lot of credit goes to him, the way he has prepared himself for the last couple of years.”Padikkal’s hundred has strengthened his case for a longer run at No. 3, even when Sai Sudharsan returns from his toe injury. Manjrekar believes his proficiency against spin makes him a strong candidate to retain the position.“On pitches where there is going to be an emphasis on spin, India should bat him at number 3 even if Sai Sudharsan comes back, because he looks such a formidable player against spin,” he said.
Article Summary: Devdutt Padikkal scored 131 not out off 178 balls against Sri Lanka. It was the 26-year-old's first Test century since Perth in Nov 2024. He became the first Indian batter to score a Test century on Independence Day. He ended a 19-Test, 35-innings wait for a No. 3 hundred.

Article Title: ‘We never give up’: Salima Tete confident India can challenge China at World Cup
Article Text:
Indian women’s hockey captain Salima Tete

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Indian women’s hockey captain Salima Tete, the message ahead of their World Cup opener against China is simple — stay confident, stick to the plan and fight until the final whistle.India begin their campaign on Sunday against World No. 4 China in Pool D at Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen, the Netherlands, knowing that a positive start could set the tone for what they hope will be a successful tournament.And while the team has spent considerable time working on its tactical game, Tete believes the focus has also been on preparing the players to handle the pressure that comes with playing on the biggest stage.“We have mainly worked on our fitness, tactical understanding and our team coordination. We have also focused a lot on improving our decision-making under pressure and being consistent throughout the match,” Tete told TOI.The captain also believes the team has learnt an important lesson from its recent experiences.“The biggest lesson is that we can compete against any strong team if we stay confident and stick to our plans.We have learned that small mistakes can make a big difference at this level, so we need to stay focused and disciplined for the full 60 minutes,” she said.That responsibility will be even greater for Tete, who will lead India into her first World Cup as captain. For the 24-year-old, it is a moment she has dreamt of, but one she also knows comes with added responsibility.“It is a very special and proud moment for me. Playing in a World Cup is a dream for every player, and leading my country as captain makes it even more special,” she said.Tete’s role, however, will extend beyond what she does on the field. She wants to ensure that the team stays united when the pressure begins to mount. “My biggest responsibility will be to lead by example, keep the team motivated and make sure that everyone stays together, especially during difficult moments,” she said.That togetherness, according to Tete, is also one of India’s biggest strengths.“I would say our biggest strength is our fighting spirit and togetherness. We never give up, and we always try to support each other. Even when things don’t go our way, we stay together and keep fighting until the final whistle,” she said.Since Sjoerd Marijne took over as head coach, India have also placed greater emphasis on structure and tactical discipline. Tete feels that work is beginning to reflect in the team’s performances.“We are becoming more confident in our style of play and are learning to adapt to different situations. I think the team is improving with every match,” she said.The first test of that progress will come against China, a side India know will demand their full attention from the opening whistle. “China are a strong team, so we need to start with confidence, stay focused on our plan and play with a lot of energy,” Tete said.For a young Indian side carrying plenty of new faces but also boasting significant experience, that balance between belief and discipline could prove crucial. And for Tete, the challenge is clear: lead from the front, keep the team together and make sure India stay in the fight for all 60 minutes.
Article Summary: India begin their World Cup campaign on Sunday against World No. 4 China. Captain Salima Tete believes the team has learnt an important lesson from its recent experiences. The 24-year-old will lead India into her first World Cup as captain.

Article Title: BWF World Championships: Beyond smashes, drops, the conditions could decide the winner
Article Text:
PV Sindhu spars with Ayush Shetty at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium. (Photo: Tanuj Lakhina)

New Delhi:

I just finished my training; I feel like there was a little bit of wind on the court, so we need to get used to the conditions. Wang Zhi Yi

Shuttlers going through the paces at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium. (Tanuj Lakhina)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Indian shuttlers going through the final touches at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi. (Photo: Tanuj Lakhina)

In badminton, a point, a set, a match and, by extension, a title, can be decided not just by a drop shot, a smash or a fake at the net. External factors such as the weather, the draft and humidity play a huge role. And that could test the players when the BWF World Championships get underway in New Delhi on Monday.With Delhi facing irregular monsoon showers and humidity hovering between 70% and 90%, the air conditioners would be cranked up over the course of the week, with the best in the business already in India. Even the non-toxic gel that has been installed to keep pigeons at bay at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium needs a certain temperature. If the arena gets warm, the gel will lose consistency and drop onto the seats below.As players arrived and practised at both the main hall and the adjacent KD Jadhav Indoor Stadium, some were met with stiff conditions, while others encountered subtle winds.A Chinese doubles shuttler mentioned that the current conditions feel different compared to the India Open in January, even though it is the same venue.Tokyo Olympics gold medallist Chen Yu Fei, who has won multiple World Championships medals but never gone all the way, stressed that she has not had the time to test the courts yet.World No. 3 Wang Zhi Yi said she noticed some movement in the air and emphasised that adjusting to the drift would be key.“For sure, I think the stadium has changed a lot; that's very good. I just finished my training; I feel like there was a little bit of wind on the court, so we need to get used to the conditions,” Wang told the media in the mixed zone.Even a modest draft from the air conditioning, fans, doors or ventilation can push the shuttle off its intended path. This affects clears, lifts, drops and smashes, so players may need to aim differently or use more controlled shots.Not everyone is complaining, though. World No. 7 Li Shifeng was pleased with how the court was behaving and landed a proverbial pat on the back for the organisers.“The size of the court is really good. I feel like the drift and all and everything, the weather including that, everything is very well maintained and very good as compared to the last time. So yeah, it's a very good place, and even the venue is very well maintained and good,” said the 26-year-old.Beyond the draft from the air conditioner, the temperature and humidity may make things trickier for the players. Over the next week, the mercury is expected to read just over 30 degrees Celsius, with humidity making things even tougher.The two factors change air density and, therefore, shuttle speed. A shuttle may travel faster in some conditions and slower in others, requiring players to adjust their power and timing. Humidity and heat also increase fatigue and dehydration risk.So when the BWF World Championships begin on Monday, watch out for the weather, the humidity and the AC, not just the speed of the smash.
Article Summary: BWF World Championships get underway in New Delhi on Monday. Delhi facing irregular monsoon showers and humidity hovering between 70% and 90%. Air conditioners would be cranked up over the course of the week, with the best in the business already in India.

Article Title: Harmanpreet brace powers India to 3-1 win over Wales in World Cup opener
Article Text:
Harmanpreet Singh scores twice as India beat Wales 3-1 (Agency Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The build-up to India’s FIH World Cup campaign had been clouded by controversies and underwhelming performances in the FIH Pro League. But at the Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen, Harmanpreet Singh and his men showed they were ready to look ahead.The Indian men’s hockey team celebrated Independence Day with a convincing 3-1 victory over Wales in their campaign opener on Saturday. Sanjay and Harmanpreet, with a brace, put their names on the scoresheet. It was a clinical performance, with India remaining calm under pressure and largely precise with their penalty-corner conversions.All three goals came from penalty corners, with India earning five of them on the day.It was somewhat odd to see the usual Men in Blue turn up in saffron, but much like the bright colour, the Indian team lit up the blue turf with a performance that will give them plenty of confidence. There were lessons too, particularly the need to convert their circle penetrations into field goals.Wales began with a bang, with Jack Pritchard forcing a save from goalkeeper Suraj Karkera in the third minute. India did not have to wait long for their first penalty corner.With their top drag-flicker Harmanpreet off the field, Sanjay stepped up and slotted home in the eighth minute, finding the gap to the right of goalkeeper Toby Reynolds-Cotterill.Harmanpreet doubled India’s advantage in the 11th minute, using deception on his drag-flick to beat Reynolds-Cotterill.India had a scare when Shilanand Lakra took a blow to his upper lip that required sutures, but the striker returned to the field. As India continued to mount pressure, Wales tried to hit on the counter but struggled to create clear opportunities. India went into the break with a 2-0 lead and continued to build on it after the change of ends.Harmanpreet completed his brace in the 43rd minute with a powerful flick, putting India firmly in control.Wales eventually breached India’s defence when Sam Welsh scored in a goalmouth melee, with Mohith scrambling to keep the ball away.Result: India 3 (Sanjay 8, Harmanpreet Singh 11, 43) bt Wales (Sam Welsh 54)
Article Summary: India beat Wales 3-1 in their FIH World Cup opener on Saturday. Sanjay and Harmanpreet Singh both scored twice for the Men in Blue. All three goals came from penalty corners, with India earning five of them on the day.

Article Title: Kush Maini eyes F1 dream as Indian driver targets strong finish to F2 season
Article Text:
Kush Maini (Image via Getty)

London: It’s been a long and bumpy ride for Kush Maini. Seven years after stepping into the world of single-seater racing, the Indian Formula 2 driver is still chasing the destination he has wanted all along: Formula 1.With five rounds remaining in F2, the ART Grand Prix driver is sixth in the standings (88 points) and feels his season has offered plenty of encouragement. Having helped ART turn around a difficult season, Maini believes he has shown enough to be ready for F1, but admits he must stand out in the final five races.“For me, F2 is going very well. I’ve definitely shown the speed. Obviously, the results probably have not been as good as the pace. With five races to go, a lot can happen. F1 is my dream. For me, it’s still very much there and that’s what I’m pushing for. I feel like I’m good enough for F1, 100%, but obviously there’re many drivers who are at this level very good and deserve a chance as well. So I’ve got to stand out in these last five races and then hopefully one day I’ll be able to achieve my dream,” said Maini, who is currently the reserve driver for Mahindra Racing at the Formula E season finale here.
Article Summary: Kush Maini believes he has shown enough to be ready for F1. Indian Formula 2 driver admits he must stand out in the final five races. Maini is currently the reserve driver for Mahindra Racing at the Formula E season finale.

Article Title: China’s long wait, PV Sindhu’s shadow: Chen Yufei, Wang Zhi Yi eye elusive Worlds gold
Article Text:
Wang Zhi Yi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: China has waited 15 years for a women’s singles World Championships gold, and in Delhi, its hopes once again rest on two formidable names, Chen Yufei and Wang Zhi Yi. Since Wang Yihan’s triumph in 2011, the title has remained beyond Chinese reach, across 10 editions. Yet the drought carries an Indian undertone – P V Sindhu. Chinese contenders have often found her standing between them and glory.Chen, the Tokyo Olympic champion and No. 4 seed, and Wang, the No. 3 seed, have repeatedly crossed Sindhu’s path. Chen leads their career rivalry 9-7; Wang holds a 4-3 edge. Yet, the Indian – seeded ninth – remains a dangerous presence, having beaten Wang at the last Worlds and carrying the aura of a big-stage specialist. At the 2025 Worlds in Paris, Wang was eliminated in the round-of-16 by Sindhu, defeating her 21-17, 21-15 in straight games.“I think I had too much on my mind before playing against Sindhu," Wang said on Saturday. She and former champion Sindhu (2019) could potentially face-off in the pre-quarterfinals. “But I think she is a good player; she just won the Japan Open title, and I think she has been playing better and better, so it’s going to be tough, but I just focus on my first match.”Her immediate opponent is Beiwen Zhang. “I don’t want to think about the result or any title; I just want to focus on the process. ”For Chen, the challenge is equally internal. “The biggest obstacle is myself. If I can conquer myself, then everything will be fine,” she said. A two-time World Championships runner-up and three-time bronze medallist, Chen has the Olympic crown but still craves the Worlds title. “You must have faith and don’t care about anything else. It is just enough,” she said.Asked about whether there's a pressure on Chinese players to win the women's singles title, Chen added: "There is no such pressure. It's just that I just have to do well. I think I will do my best in every match and try to win. It is about ourselves, how we prepare for the event, not for some specific players."Conditions at the refurbished Indira Gandhi (IG) indoor stadium will add another layer. After Saturday’s training, Wang said, “I feel like there was a little bit of wind on the court, so we need to get used to the conditions.” Chen was more reassuring: “The conditions are quite good compared to the last time we played here,” though she admitted, “the weather is not comfortable.”Both, however, appeared satisfied after their opening sessions. But the real test will come when the championships begin on Monday. The Worlds is returning to Indian shores after a gap of 17 years, with the best players looking forward to getting their hands on the coveted title. This time, the Badminton Association of India (BA) has taken some extra steps, learning from the lessons learnt during the controversy-marred India Open in Jan, and even made a sanitary pad machine available for women players, female support staff and officials and spectators.
Article Summary: China has waited 15 years for a women's singles World Championships gold. Since Wang Yihan’s triumph in 2011, the title has remained beyond Chinese reach. The drought carries an Indian undertone – P V Sindhu. Chen leads their career rivalry 9-7; Wang holds a 4-3 edge.

Article Title: State associations urge sports ministry to ensure early EFI elections
Article Text:
Union Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya felicitates Mirabai Chanu Saikhom (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: The Indian States Equestrian Association (IESA) on Saturday urged the ministry of youth affairs and sports (MYAS) and the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) to take urgent steps to conduct the long-pending elections to the executive committee of the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI).At a hybrid meeting attended by representatives of equestrian associations from 25 states and Union Territories, the IESA recalled that it had suggested before the Delhi High Court that the IOA appoint an ad hoc committee and complete the election process within three months.“Sadly, despite the lapse of three months since the ad hoc committee was appointed on March 27, 2026, there are no signs of elections being held to the executive committee of the EFI,” Rajasthan Equestrian Association president Raghavendra Singh Dundlod said.The state associations also urged the IOA to include equestrian sport in the National Games schedule and the sports ministry to make the discipline an integral part of the Khelo India Youth Games, citing its growing popularity and India’s performances at international competitions.“The meeting took into account the fact that India has won 14 medals in the Asian Games and five in the Asian Equestrian Championships,” Dundlod said.He added that several state governments reward athletes and offer appointments only to those who have represented their respective states.The IESA also called upon the IOA-appointed ad hoc committee to make public records of all meetings held by it and its sub-committees.“There have been many policy decisions, including selection criteria, event allocation and hike in fees, that the ad hoc committee has made without securing approval of the EFI general body,” Dundlod said.The state associations were also apprised of their responsibilities under the National Sports Governance Act 2025 and the National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules 2026. They agreed to take necessary remedial measures at the earliest to ensure eligibility for registration with the National Sports Board once the body becomes functional.
Article Summary: The Indian States Equestrian Association (IESA) on Saturday urged the ministry of youth affairs and sports (MYAS) and the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) to take urgent steps to conduct the long-pending elections. The IESA recalled that it had suggested before the Delhi High Court that the IOA appoint an ad hoc committee and complete the election process within three months.

Article Title: Jamshedpur FC seal final quarter-final berth on last day of Durand Cup group stage
Article Text:
Lawmsangzuala after scoring during the Durand Cup. (Pic Credit: Durand Cup Media)

Quarterfinal line-up:

KOLKATA: The last of group stage matches – that were played across three different venues in the east – lived up to its billing as Jamshedpur FC produced a last-day 6-0 rout to make the quarters, Shillong Lajong and Langsning FC enthralled the crowd with a gripping 3-3 draw while Bodoland FC, who were already out of contention for the knockouts, bowed out with a dominating 6-0 thrashing of their local rivals Karbi Anglong Morning Star FC.The star of the day was a teenager playing his first senior tournament for Jamshedpur FC at the 135th Durand Cup – 17-year-old Lawmsangzuala, nicknamed ‘Mama’. The Jamshedpur FC Academy product, who had made his way through the club ranks, came on as a substitute at Birsa Munda Football Stadium in Ranchi and scored a memorable hat-trick that made the Red Miners the last team to qualify for the quarterfinals.They did have to wait for the result of the Shillong derby in an evening fixture at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium where a win for Langsning could have helped them qualify ahead of rivals Lajong and end Jamshedpur’s hopes of progress.However, despite a frantic effort of their attackers, who had already ensured a late comeback draw, for a last-ditch winner was put paid to by the Shillong Lajong defenders.The draw meant that Lajong had qualified from Group E as toppers while Jamshedpur made their way – behind Group C leaders SC Delhi – as the second second-placed qualifiers after East Bengal.Earlier, at Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium in Guwahati, skipper Holicharan Narzary led Bodoland FC from the front with four goals in their last game, an inconsequential fixture in Group F with NorthEast United FC having already qualified on top.
Article Summary: Lawmsangzuala scored a hat-trick in Jamshedpur FC's last-day 6-0 rout. Shillong Lajong and Langsning FC enthralled the crowd with a gripping 3-3 draw. Bodoland FC, who were already out of contention for the knockouts, bowed out with a dominating6-0 thrashing of local rivals Karbi Anglong Morning Star FC.

Article Title: Subroto Cup to kick off on August 18; 107 teams to compete across three age categories
Article Text:
Air Marshal S. Sivakumar during the official announcement event for 65th Subroto Cup. (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The 65th edition of the prestigious Subroto Cup International Football Tournament will kick off on August 18, with 107 teams set to compete across three age categories in New Delhi NCR and Bengaluru.The tournament, organised by the Subroto Mukerjee Sports Education Society (SMSES) under the aegis of the Air Force Sports Control Board, will be held until Sept 24. The competition will feature Junior Girls (U-17), Sub-Junior Boys (U-15) and Junior Boys (U-17), with more than 215 matches scheduled across the three categories.The official announcement was made on Wednesday in the presence of Air Marshal S. Sivakumar VSM, Air Officer-in-Charge Administration and Vice Chairman of SMSES, who attended as the chief guest. Former India footballer Ashalata Devi Loitongbam was also present as the guest of honour.“The Indian Air Force and SMSES are committed to making the tournament bigger and better every year, providing a platform for young athletes to take the next step in their careers,” Sivakumar said.The Junior Girls (U-17) competition will open the tournament in New Delhi, NCR, from Aug 18 to 27. The Sub-Junior Boys (U-15) category will be held in Bengaluru from Sept 1 to 9, before the Junior Boys (U-17) competition concludes the tournament in New Delhi NCR from Sept 15 to 24.Teams representing various states, Union Territories and educational bodies will participate, with Sri Lanka providing international representation. An age-determination test will also be conducted for the Sub-Junior Boys category in Bengaluru to ensure a level playing field.The matches will be played at venues including Ambedkar Stadium, Tejas Football Ground, Subroto Park Football Ground, Pinto Park Football Ground and Rajokri Football Ground in the Delhi-NCR region. In Bengaluru, Air Force School Jalahalli, Air Force School Yelahanka and Subroto Football Ground Jalahalli will host matches.Farook Higher Secondary School of Kerala is the defending champion in the Junior Boys' category, while Betkuchi High School of Guwahati (Assam) holds the Junior Girls' title. Minerva Public School (CISCE) is the reigning Sub-Junior Boys champion.First held in 1960, the Subroto Cup was conceived by Air Marshal Subroto Mukerjee to promote grassroots football across India.
Article Summary: The 65th edition of the prestigious Subroto Cup International Football Tournament will kick off on August 18. 107 teams will compete across three age categories in New Delhi NCR and Bengaluru. Former India footballer Ashalata Devi Loitongbam was the guest of honour at the official announcement event.

Article Title: Kuldeep, Jadeja, Suthar: Will India play three left-arm spinners in Galle? Coach drops hint
Article Text:
Kuldeep Yadav, Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India could field three left-arm spinners in the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, with bowling coach Morne Morkel saying Kuldeep Yadav Ravindra Jadeja and Manav Suthar offer different skills and can form an attacking bowling combination.Kuldeep brings left-arm wrist spin and an attacking option, Jadeja relies on accuracy, while Suthar bowls a more traditional left-arm spin.“Kuldeep is there, and he's the attacking sort of bowler and for us, his experience and class can't look past. So yeah, I think for us they're all different in their way,” Morkel told the media here on Thursday.“So one (Suthar) turns a bit more, one (Jadeja) is slightly more accurate and I don't think it's a (three left-arm spinners) massive concern for us.“It’s just how Gill is going to use those guys at certain times. But yeah, I mean in terms of skill they've got the skill to get the 20 wickets for us,” he added.Morkel said the Galle pitch could also support the decision to play three spinners, with conditions expected to become more helpful to spin as the Test progresses.“Traditionally also if you look at the venue how it stacks and how it's been played up, that's sort of the way (three spinners) to go I think.The way we go with our spin bowling attack or spinners, it’s a very attacking option.“But looking at the surface, you know, to me, looks like a good surface, and I think as the Test goes on, you know, something will start to happen.“So, we've prepared for all that can come our way, as it is more about the mental challenge in playing these conditions, batting time, bowling those spells and getting the ball in the right areas,” he detailed.India are also deciding on their second seamer alongside Mohammed Siraj. The choice is between Gurnoor Brar and Prasidh Krishna, both of whom have limited Test experience.Morkel said either player would be ready if selected.“I think it's exciting. They've played a lot of cricket back home where it's also tough bowling conditions, and I think coming here the biggest challenge will be the heat and humidity."
Article Summary: Kuldeep Yadav, Ravindra Jadeja and Manav Suthar offer different skills and can form an attacking bowling combination, says bowling coach Morne Morkel. Morkel said the Galle pitch could also support the decision to play three spinners, with conditions expected to become more helpful to spin.

Article Title: Devdutt Padikkal or Sai Sudharsan? Manjrekar makes no. 3 call: 'He looks such a formidable player'

Padikkal makes most of No. 3 opportunity

Devdutt Padikkal made a strong statement in India's first Test against Sri Lanka, dominating the opening day in Galle and strengthening his case for a permanent place at No. 3. Drafted into the playing XI after Sai Sudharsan was ruled out with an injury, Padikkal produced a magnificent unbeaten 131 on Day 1. He looked completely at ease against Sri Lanka's spinners and helped India finish the rain-curtailed opening day on 288/2 after 73 overs.His performance has now earned high praise from former India batter Sanjay Manjrekar , who believes Padikkal's ability against spin makes him an ideal No. 3 option for India even after Sudharsan returns.While Padikkal was compiling his century, Manjrekar took to X to highlight the batter's impressive technique against spin.“Devdutt Padikkal god sent for India v spinners. Excellent technique, both in defence & attack.”Manjrekar later elaborated on Padikkal's strengths during a discussion on Sony Sports, pointing to his ability to combine defence, strike rotation and attacking strokes against spin.“Devdutt Padikkal was the big change that India had, I really think selection is so good that when you see Padikkal walk in and play spin so comfortably, because he's good in defense against spin, he's good at picking 1s and 2s when the field is slightly deep, and then he's also good at playing attacking shots, and that too off the back foot on slow, turning pitches, ” Manjrekar said.Padikkal repeatedly used the depth of the crease to negate Sri Lanka's spinners while also stepping out whenever the bowlers offered him an opportunity. One of the standout moments came when he charged Prabath Jayasuriya and lofted the left-arm spinner over long-on for a six.For Manjrekar, however, it was Padikkal's ability to score off the back foot on a slow, turning surface that particularly impressed him.“That's something remarkable. On slow, turning pitches, to hit shots off the back foot with a straight bat and the pull shot tells you that it's somebody who wants to get onto the back foot, and the best way to play spin on a slow, turning pitch is to play the majority of the bowling off the back foot, ” he added.“Along with that, he's also got this knack of going down the pitch and hitting the ball over the sight screen. So on pitches where there is going to be an emphasis on spin, India should bat him at number 3 even if Sai Sudharsan comes back, because he looks such a formidable player against spin, I think it was godsent for India, Devdutt Padikkal at No. 3 with the kind of spin talent he has,” Manjrekar said.Padikkal was handed the No. 3 role following Sudharsan's injury and responded with a career-defining performance. His unbeaten 131 also made him the first Indian batter to score a Test century on Independence Day, while he became only the second Indian cricketer after Virat Kohli to score an international century on August 15.
Article Summary: Devdutt Padikkal scores unbeaten 131 in India's first Test against Sri Lanka. Former India batter Sanjay Manjrekar hails 'godsent for India' against spin. ManJrekar praises PadikkAl's ability to score off the back foot on slow, turning pitches.

Article Title: ‘Desire to play is not a problem’: Azhar Ali on Pakistan’s Test cricket downfall
Article Text:

Former Pakistan captain Azhar Ali has linked the country’s recent struggles in Test cricket to the decline of departmental cricket, which he believes played a major role in developing players.Azhar, who represented Pakistan in nine Tests and 31 ODIs, described departmental teams as a key “nursery” for the national side and warned that the system is once again being weakened.“Department cricket is a big need for Pakistan,” Azhar told Cricinfo.He said shutting down the system had hurt the development of Pakistani cricket and that its return has not been given enough importance.The Pakistan Cricket Board recently removed WAPDA and Sahir Associates from the 2026-27 domestic season after the teams did not meet new regulations. WAPDA had been one of Pakistan’s longest-running domestic teams.Azhar also criticised the PCB for frequently changing its domestic structure instead of allowing a system time to work.“The first thing I'd do is to give any system we implement a few years. If you change every year, then you were either wrong last year, or you're wrong now,” he said.Azhar himself developed through departmental cricket and believes it provided young players with something crucial: financial security.“I was moulded in department cricket, as so many others have been,” Azhar said.He explained that departmental teams offered salaries even when regional teams overlooked players, allowing cricketers to continue pursuing the sport.Azhar said Pakistan has no shortage of youngsters who want to play cricket, but many families cannot afford to let them pursue it without financial support.“Desire to play is not a problem [in Pakistan],” he said.He added that cricket must be financially viable for young players, especially those who need to support their families.“It's easy to say, reduce the teams in domestic cricket. But if you're not getting financially rewarded for it, how many kids will be able to afford to take up cricket?” Azhar said.He warned that without such support, talented youngsters could abandon cricket or leave Pakistan in search of better opportunities.

The Pakistan Cricket Board recently removed WAPDA and Sahir Associates from the 2026-27 domestic season. Azhar described departmental teams as a key ‘nursery’ for the national side.

Article Title: ‘The way he has prepared himself’: India coach explains key to Devdutt Padikkal’s maiden Test century

Devdutt Padikkal plays a shot during day one of the first Test against Sri Lanka. (AP Photo)

Back-foot game key to Padikkal's success

No. 3 debate remains open

Sri Lanka also impressed by Padikkal

NEW DELHI: India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak credited Devdutt Padikkal's preparation and improved back-foot game after the left-hander produced a composed unbeaten 131 to put India in a strong position on the opening day of the first Test against Sri Lanka. Padikkal, batting at No. 3, brought up his maiden international hundred as India reached 288 for two at stumps.Padikkal's innings was built around calculated shot selection and an ability to adapt to Sri Lanka's spin-heavy attack. Kotak said the 26-year-old had specifically worked on his back-foot game during his preparations at the BCCI Centre of Excellence, while also developing his options against turning deliveries.“I am so happy for him because he was actually waiting for his opportunity. The way he played here and in the warm-up match, it's really encouraging,” Kotak said at the post-day press conference.Kotak explained that Padikkal's preparation had focused on developing multiple ways of putting pressure on spinners, particularly when the pitch offered turn. The batter's ability to move back and create room, combined with occasional use of the sweep and charge down the track, allowed him to keep Sri Lanka's bowlers from settling into a rhythm.“Preparation, I would say, overall the way Devdutt, was preparing and I saw it in the NCA (BCCI CoE)…he was working on his back foot game. We try that when we expect a turn from a pitch.“We also tried to work on step-out, sweep besides the back foot game. So, a lot of credit goes to him, the way he has prepared himself for the last couple of years,” he added.Padikkal's innings reflected that preparation. He was predominantly comfortable playing off the back foot but was also willing to step out when he needed to dominate the spinners.Padikkal's century could also add another dimension to India's selection decisions once regular No. 3 Sai Sudharsan returns from his toe injury. Kotak, however, suggested the team is less concerned about rigid batting positions and more focused on how players adapt to match situations.“I think Devdutt batted really well. So Sai also has been batting really well at that number. But the thing is they all are new ball batsmen. So they open, they go number three, so, we are very flexible.“But I would look at the way they bat, how they are adapting to conditions, how they are dealing with the different stages of a match, and that is very important for me rather than number three or four or five,” he added.Padikkal's performance drew praise from Sri Lanka's spin and fielding coach Jordan Gregory, who felt the Indian batter and KL Rahul had successfully put pressure back on the hosts. Rahul also made a significant contribution before retiring hurt.“I think firstly, credit to Padikkal. I think that he batted superbly today and so did KL. Unfortunate for him to get injured,” Gregory said.Gregory also praised debutant off-spinner Keshara Nuwantha for the way he handled the challenge of bowling against India's batters.“It’s very encouraging to see that Kesh on his debut had asked a lot of questions and created a lot of opportunities.“So credit to him. I could imagine there may have been a couple of nerves from his side. But I'm very proud of him and the way he bowled on his debut,” he added.
Article Summary: Devdutt Padikkal scores unbeaten 131 as India reach 288 for two at stumps on day one of first Test against Sri Lanka. India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak credits PadikkAl's preparation and improved back-foot game. Sri Lanka's spin and fielding coach Jordan Gregory also praised Padikal and KL Rahul.

Article Title: ‘You can’t do that’: David Warner slams Steve Smith over bizarre review against Bangladesh
Article Text:
Steve Smith (Image: ANI)

Warner questions Smith’s quick review

Smith involved in another strange moment

Former Australia opener David Warner criticised Steve Smith for an unusual review during the first Test against Bangladesh on Saturday. Warner said he had no issue with Smith challenging the umpire’s decision, but questioned why the Australian batter signalled for a review before umpire Kumar Dharmasena had even raised his finger.The incident happened in the 14th over with Australia at 40/2. Ebadot Hossain bowled outside off and Smith attempted a big drive. A sound was heard as the ball passed the bat, prompting Hossain and wicketkeeper Litton Das to appeal.As Dharmasena began raising his finger, Smith immediately made the ‘T’ signal for a review.“I just don’t like the way that Steve’s reacted there," Warner said on air. “You can’t do that."When commentator Brendon Julian pointed out that Smith appeared certain he had not been dismissed and had taken an extremely quick review, Warner repeated, “I just don’t think you can do that!"Former Australia spinner Kerry O’Keeffe also described the incident as highly unusual.“That is a unique moment in Test cricket that a batter has gone upstairs before the umpire has made a decision," he said.The review eventually proved Smith’s instinct correct. Replays and ECHO edge technology showed that the sound came from Smith’s bat hitting the ground rather than an edge.It was not the first unusual incident involving Smith, Hossain and Dharmasena in the match. Earlier in Australia’s innings, Hossain believed he had dismissed Smith caught behind, and Smith even started walking back.However, Dharmasena did not give him out.Bangladesh reviewed the decision, but technology showed no edge. Smith later admitted that he believed he had made contact.“I think so, yeah," Smith said.Asked if he had been fortunate to survive, Smith replied, “I was lucky? Yeah, it seems that way. You got to take it sometimes."Smith was eventually dismissed for 44 off 88 balls, edging Mehidy Hasan Miraz. Australia finished the day in trouble, trailing Bangladesh by 67 runs with four wickets remaining.
Article Summary: Former Australia opener David Warner criticised Steve Smith for an unusual review during the first Test against Bangladesh. Warner questioned why the Australian batter signalled for a review before umpire Kumar Dharmasena had even raised his finger. The incident happened in the 14th over with Australia at 40/2.

Article Title: Devdutt Padikkal's 131 headlines India's dominant Day 1 at 288/2 in Galle on Independence Day

Padikkal completes maiden Test century

Gill falls, Pant joins Padikkal

Devdutt Padikkal stole the spotlight on a memorable opening day as India finished 288/2 against Sri Lanka in the first Test at the Galle International Cricket Stadium on Saturday. On a rain-interrupted day that marked India's 600th Test match, Padikkal produced a sublime unbeaten 131 to put India firmly in control. Rishabh Pant was unbeaten on 27 at stumps, while Sri Lanka's bowlers struggled to make an impact on a pitch offering some assistance to spin.India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bat first. Yashasvi Jaiswal provided an aggressive start before his innings was cut short by a costly mix-up with KL Rahul. Jaiswal, who had raced to 32, was run out as India lost their first wicket for 47.Padikkal then joined Rahul at the crease after coming into the playing XI at No. 3 following Sai Sudharsan's injury setback. The pair steadied India's innings and guided the visitors to 101/1 before rain forced an early lunch break.After the resumption, Padikkal and Rahul took control of the contest. The Karnataka duo negotiated Sri Lanka's spin attack with confidence, rotating the strike and finding the boundaries whenever opportunities presented themselves.Both batters brought up their half-centuries as their partnership grew rapidly.By the tea interval, India had reached 197/1, with Padikkal and Rahul having added 150 runs for the second wicket.However, Rahul's excellent innings came to an unfortunate end when he was forced to retire hurt on 77 after suffering severe cramps and discomfort in his right hand. Rahul's knock came from 162 balls and included nine fours and a six.With Rahul off the field, Gill joined Padikkal in the middle. The left-hander continued to dictate terms and accelerated against the Sri Lankan attack. Padikkal brought up his maiden Test century off 134 balls, celebrating a landmark moment in his young Test career.His century was particularly significant as he became the first Indian batter to score a Test hundred on Independence Day and only the second Indian to score an international century on August 15 after Virat Kohli. Padikkal also became only the second Indian left-hander in the 21st century to score a Test century from No. 3, after Sourav Ganguly.Gill's stay at the crease was brief as he was dismissed for 16, with Prabath Jayasuriya providing Sri Lanka with their only bowler-credited wicket of the day. Rishabh Pant then joined Padikkal and immediately injected momentum into the innings, finishing unbeaten on 27 off 36 balls, with three fours and a six.Padikkal remained unbeaten on 131 off 178 balls, having struck 12 fours and a six. The pair added an unbeaten 52-run partnership as India reached 288/2 in 73 overs at stumps.
Article Summary: Devdutt Padikkal scores unbeaten 131 to put India firmly in control. Rishabh Pant was unbeaten on 27 at stumps, while Sri Lanka's bowlers struggled to make an impact on a pitch offering some assistance to spin. India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bat first.

Article Title: A ton of class! Devdutt Padikkal makes the long wait count
Article Text:
Devdutt Padikkal celebrates after scoring his maiden Test century at Galle. (Photo: BCCI | X)

Timesofindia.com in Galle:

Devdutt Padikkal

Brief Scores

Quick single, a punch in the air followed by a jubilant jump before unleashing another punch. The helmet came off in a flash, and his arms spread wide to acknowledge the applause from the dressing room and the spectators braving the heat on the grass banks. It was a memorable moment for Devdutt Padikkal, who notched up his maiden Test hundred, and it couldn't have come at a better time, both for him and the country.Playing a Test for the country after 632 days, he walked into bat after a moment of chaos between Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul , who were involved in a terrible mix-up, but took the mantle seamlessly from the opener. Devdutt got off the mark with a boundary, danced down the track to launch Prabath Jayasuriya for a maximum early in the innings and showcased excellent footwork against both spin and pace. There wasn't much happening off the surface in the first session, but the odd delivery did surprise the batters, mostly because of the drift caused by the crosswinds.Off-spinner Keshara Nuwantha, introduced in the ninth over on his debut, got one to drift in and hold its line after pitching, but the bounce saved Devdutt, who wore a look of disbelief. No one expected that kind of assistance from the surface that early in the contest, and the remainder of the day showed that what happened in the 13th over was an anomaly.Except for the occasional delivery with more drift than usual, there wasn't much turn on offer, and Devdutt remained very busy and breezy in his approach, outscoring his senior partner, Rahul, with ease.Like the spinners, pacers Lahiru Kumara and Asitha Fernando also found little assistance. The two had their moments, but their effort wasn't consistent enough to challenge the visitors in the beautiful batting conditions. After the first rain break, Asitha bowled a testing spell to both Rahul and Devdutt, but both were seasoned enough to navigate the period, when moisture might have seeped into the surface because of the strong shower, and then feasted on some ordinary bowling.While Rahul was happy to switch to blockathon mode, Devdutt kept the board moving at a fair clip. The Karnataka batters, who spend a lot of time off the field bonding over their mutual love for coffee, complemented each other really well. Rahul, who unfortunately retired hurt due to cramps, enjoys batting with Devdutt as the left-hander's positive approach allows him to switch to zen mode.Devdutt remained in the driving seat of the 150-run stand, which put India in a dominant position on the opening day, maximizing the crucial toss Shubman Gill had won earlier. With the pitch expected to deteriorate in the coming days, India's best shot at winning the Test is to bat once and bat big, and both Devdutt and Rahul laid a solid foundation for that.A couple of weeks ago, Devdutt was nowhere close to the playing XI, but an ill-timed injury to Sai Sudharsan opened up the No. 3 slot. The management, not leaving anything to last-minute chaos, had asked Devdutt to be ready, and the Karnataka batter was mentally in the zone to make the chance count. For over a year now, he has spent a lot of time working on his game against spin, and domination has remained the keyword.This domination even caught the eye of chief selector Ajit Agarkar, who was also in the stands in Galle during a Ranji Trophy game between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu in 2024. Devdutt has only taken his game up several notches since his debut in the home series against England, and even though opportunities remained few and far between, the work continued behind the scenes. The 26-year-old identified the No. 3 slot as his own, even though his Test debut occurred at No. 4.In the 2025-26 season, where he also took over as captain from Mayank Agarwal, Padikkal stuck to the No. 3 spot except for one game against Punjab. He returned with a tournament haul of 543 runs in six games, a massive improvement from the 129 runs in four games during the 2024-25 edition. Role clarity, leadership responsibility and domination against spin worked in his favour as he signalled his readiness for game time with the Test team.The outing in Galle has ensured that whenever Sai regains match fitness, he will not be a straightforward pick in the Playing XI and will always have a ready Devdutt breathing down his neck.288 for 2 after 73 overs (Devdutt Padikkal 131 not out, KLRahul 77 retired hurt; Prabath Jayasuriya 1/77)
Article Summary: Devdutt Padikkal scores maiden Test century for India in first Test at Galle. Karnataka batsman joins KL Rahul in 150-run stand to put India in dominant position. India won the toss and opted to bat first after winning the toss.

Devdutt Padikkal marked his return to India's Test setup in style, smashing his maiden Test century during the first Test against Sri Lanka at the Galle International Cricket Stadium. The left-hander, who has won two IPL titles with Royal Challengers Bengaluru, produced a fluent and assured knock at No. 3 to make a strong case for himself in India's middle order.Padikkal became only the second Indian left-handed batter in the 21st century to score a Test century from No. 3, after former captain Sourav Ganguly. Ganguly had scored 136 against Zimbabwe in Delhi in 2002.Overall, Padikkal is the sixth Indian left-hander to score a Test hundred from the No. 3 position. The list is led by Vinod Kambli with four centuries, followed by Ganguly with three, while Salim Durani, Bapu Nadkarni, Ajit Wadekar, Eknath Solkar, Surinder Amarnath and now Padikkal have one each.Padikkal's century also ended a prolonged wait for an Indian batter to score a Test hundred from No. 3. The last Indian to achieve the feat was Shubman Gill , who scored a century against Bangladesh in Chennai in September 2024.Since then, India had used seven different batters at No. 3 across 19 Tests, with the position collectively averaging just 27.28 and producing only five scores of 50 or more in 35 innings.The 25-year-old had also enjoyed a productive 2025-26 Ranji Trophy season, averaging 60.33, and carried that confidence into Galle. Article Title: Rajasthan stuck in 2012, Manipur in 2023: How actively are states with CWG medals promoting sports?
Article Text:
Are sports bodies of Indian states promoting the game properly?

Haryana: Hit on the podium, not so much off it

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Social media presence Local sports events Government funding 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.No state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Facebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.And yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. It’s the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.If there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Its X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Gulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.Delhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.Set against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.Not every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation Silence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.
Article Summary: India won 39 medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Haryana produced 11 medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze. But the state sports department has posted just once in all of 2026. What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Government funding or social media presence? Share your view.

Article Title: ‘That video was not ordinary’: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi shares a light moment with boxer Lovlina Borgohain. (PTI Photo)

‘That video was not ordinary’

NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.“Kya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)” Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.“We had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,” she explained.Modi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.“To be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,” he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics. Modi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.“Itne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),” Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.“I was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.“There were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,” she said.The meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.“During the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),” he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.“I have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.“Far more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,” Modi said.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time. India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.

Article Title: ‘From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping’: PM Modi’s heartfelt message to CWG heroes - Watch
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi interacted with India's CWG 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday. (Pic credit: PM Modi's X post)

Mirabai recalls four years of struggle

‘One family will bring three medals’

India’s Glasgow success

NEW DELHI: “From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping.”Prime Minister Narendra Modi had an emotional message for Mirabai Chanu as he interacted with India's Commonwealth Games 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday, reflecting on the sacrifices behind the country's successful campaign in Glasgow.Modi hosted the medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg and heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys at the Games. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings.During one of the conversations, Modi recalled the emotional scenes surrounding Mirabai's gold-medal triumph.“Tears were falling from you. I feel as if from every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping,” Modi told the Olympic silver medallist.Mirabai, who won gold in Glasgow, opened up about the difficult journey that preceded her Commonwealth Games triumph, including the disappointment of the Paris Olympics.“I was very happy, and emotional too. That day the happiness was greater and I cried because at the Paris Olympics, I lost a medal by 1 kg. In a player’s life what all we have to face. So within these 4 years, how much and what all I had faced, every time injuries were going on and all that was happening.So with great difficulty I had faced these 4 years. So when all that happened, on the podium when I stood, sir, and when our flag goes up and our national anthem plays, sir, we cannot stop, sir, tears come out on their own,” she said.Modi responded by highlighting the wider impact of the athletes' achievements.“This is very good. It is not as if this achievement of yours is considered only your achievement; your victory becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations.”The informal interaction also saw athletes share lighter and deeply personal moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Modi reminded para shot put gold medallist Sharmila Dhankar of a promise she had made earlier.“You made a promise. Last time, yours, both daughters will become players,” Modi said with a smile.Dhankar replied: “Haanji, right now they are young in age. In the next Commonwealth, one family will bring 3 medals.”Men's 100m T47 gold medallist Dilip Gavit, meanwhile, spoke about dedicating his performance to his guru.“When I was running, when my event was on 29th (July), that day was Guru Purnima, so that day I gave a gift to my guru,” he was heard saying in the video.In another video posted by Modi, gold medallist boxer Sakshi Chaudhary introduced herself and the contingent.“Hello friends! This is Sakshi Chaudhary. Today, our honourable Prime Minister has invited us, the Commonwealth Games medalists, and we feel very proud. We are extremely happy to have met him; he is very humble. Sir, would you like to say something?” she said.Modi replied with a message that summed up his interaction with the athletes: “Jo khelega, woh khilega” (The one who plays, will blossom). “Always cheer for Bharat.”India's fourth-place finish came despite a significantly smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme compared to Birmingham 2022. India sent 122 athletes to Glasgow, compared to 210 in Birmingham, while 30 of its 61 medals in 2022 came in sports that were not part of the Glasgow programme.Despite those limitations, India retained its fourth-place position and improved its medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with medals. Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh was the only Indian athlete to win two medals.The Glasgow Games concluded after 11 days, with Scotland handing over the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India ahead of the 2030 edition in Ahmedabad.The symbols were handed to Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi during the closing ceremony.Ahmedabad will become only the second Indian city to host the Commonwealth Games after New Delhi staged the 2010 edition.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi hosted medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg. Modi heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze.
